# PR #4739: Patch: a job ran over 10 minutes

Closes #4721

# What changed

`scripts/ci-shards.toml`: `[rust-test]` `"tools, wasm" = 4` becomes `= 8`, with the entry's comment rewritten (new #4721 times, why 8, pin note). One file, no Rust touched.

No test needed a daily-move, so Step 5 of the plan was skipped with measurements: every test in the two reported slow shards (old `1/4`, 514 tests; old `4/4`, 526 tests) was timed locally on this 2-core box, which is slower per core than CI's 4-core runners. The slowest are `fork_screen`'s `r4607000_resume_refuses_a_changed_header_before_any_game` (90 s), `r4607000_a_finished_save_plays_nothing_and_reprints_its_tally` (86 s) and `r4607000_a_deal_finished_before_a_batch_error_stays_in_the_file` (68 s). All 253 other `jackioh`-bin tests run in 41 s or less, and every other binary of the old shards finishes its whole share in 46 s. Nothing is over the 180 s rule, so a count alone fixes it.

# How you tested it

- Listed the group's tests exactly as CI does (`cargo test --workspace --exclude ... -- --skip fuzz:: --skip selfplay:: --skip positions:: --list`), reproduced `shard 1 4` / `shard 4 4`, and ran both full shards to green (6m01s, 3m33s wall locally).
- Timed the plan's named suspects plus every remaining `jackioh`-bin test individually (all exit 0; maxima above).
- `python3 .github/ci/matrix.py matrix` now lists `tools, wasm 1/8` through `8/8`; all 2110 test names land in exactly one K=8 shard. The three slowest tests spread across shards (90 s + 32 s in 5/8, 86 s + 41 s + 22 s in 8/8, 68 s + 33 s + 13 s in 1/8), so no shard inherits the old shape.
- Ran the three slowest K=8 shards fully to green locally: 8/8 in 3m03s, 5/8 in 2m38s, 1/8 in 2m19s; warm-cache list build takes 3 s. Slowest shard budgets ~3 min locally with headroom to the 8-minute TARGET, so the Step 9 contingency (compile-bound group) did not trigger.
- `cargo fmt --check` passes; `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes with no warnings. `cargo jackioh spec check` not needed: no ruling note added or cited (the comment names the same R-ids the old one did).

# Decisions

- Count to 8 rather than daily-moving anything: with no test over 180 s, the 12–13 min shards were the sum of many small tests, which a count splits. Rejected daily-moving the 90 s/86 s/68 s fork-screen tests because the rule is 180 s and each already has per-PR coverage in the binary.
- 8 is `MAX_SHARDS`, the most a count may be; the web unit job already runs at 8. Rejected any other count: only 8 matches the pin below.

# Person-side half

The bot may not edit `bot/`. Until a person applies this, `bot selftest` is red, which is expected. In `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py`:

- The comment `` `tools, wasm` four since #4432 `` becomes `` `tools, wasm` eight since #4721 ``.
- The JOBS entries `"tools, wasm 1/4", "tools, wasm 2/4", "tools, wasm 3/4", "tools, wasm 4/4",` become `"tools, wasm 1/8", "tools, wasm 2/8", "tools, wasm 3/8", "tools, wasm 4/8", "tools, wasm 5/8", "tools, wasm 6/8", "tools, wasm 7/8", "tools, wasm 8/8",`.
- `jobs["tools, wasm 1/4"]` becomes `jobs["tools, wasm 1/8"]`.
- `{(1, 1), (1, 4), (2, 4), (3, 4), (4, 4)}` becomes `{(1, 1), (1, 4), (2, 4), (3, 4), (4, 4), (1, 8), (2, 8), (3, 8), (4, 8), (5, 8), (6, 8), (7, 8), (8, 8)}`.

- Each new keeper from Step 5, named `<same-ruling>_a_hand_written_<thing>_without_playing` after the #4690 example; it asserts the daily-moved test's wiring without playing games and fails if the tally/save/edge format changes.
- The daily-moved tests themselves: run once with `--ignored` to confirm they still pass (`cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh -- --exact <name> --ignored`), proving the daily `super.yml` legs still hold them.
- `python3 .github/ci/matrix.py matrix` plus the K=8 shard-distribution check from Step 7 (every test in exactly one shard).
- `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh <keeper>`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

- [ ] Every test over 180 s in the old slow shards is daily-moved with a playing-no-games keeper, or Step 4 measured none over the threshold.
- [ ] `scripts/ci-shards.toml` has `"tools, wasm" = 8` with the rewritten comment.

- [ ] Keeper tests, `fmt`, and `clippy` pass; moved tests pass with `--ignored`.
- [ ] The PR description carries the exact `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py` diff and the request for a person to apply it; the builder changed nothing under `.github/`, `bot/`, `.harness/`, or `.squishy/`.
- [ ] The contingency (Step 9) was either not triggered or handed to a person with measurements.

## Risks

- Hash collision: two remaining slow tests can land in one K=8 shard; Step 7 checks the real distribution and Step 5 removes the slower one, so no shard inherits the old 12-minute shape.
- Compile-bound group: each shard recompiles the same workspace subset, so if the warm-cache build alone fills the budget, no count suffices; Step 9 escalates to a person with numbers instead of shipping a futile bump.
- Dropped coverage: `#[ignore]` tests vanish from PR runs; the `daily:` reason plus the `--ignored` run keeps them in `super.yml`'s daily legs, and each keeper holds the wiring per PR.
- No game-logic, determinism, replay, or hidden-information risk: the change moves or shards tests only; no engine, card, AI, or view code changes.

## Open questions

- A person must apply the `bot/tests/test_ci_matrix.py` pin from Step 10 before `bot selftest` (and hence the PR) can go green; the builder cannot do this part.
